g.text: pattern ownership, and lifecycle entry points.
Runtime setup, PLC signal translation, cycle
During runtime, controller calls are queued and the
A50 adds explicit taskState transitions around
Runtime reconnect behavior is delegated to explicit
recovery policies per device role. Reconnect is
UNLIMITED: a lost role withdraws bTaskReady, retries
until it returns or the runtime ends, and never
escalates to a fault. Consequence for the PLC: a dead
link shows bTaskReady=false with bTaskFault=false, so
bTaskFault is the wrong signal to watch for it.
Recovery/fault signals now feed the task state machine.
The controller does not call TaskLocalization directly.
It receives an immutable RuntimeContext snapshot at setup,
coordinates device runners through queued APIs, and emits
runtimeMatchingRequested() so matching runs on the task
A latched cycle fault always has a way out: a bErrorReset
rising edge, or automatically after kFaultAutoRecoverMs
(2000 ms) when no acknowledge arrives. Both run one shared
unconditional; re-arming still validates roles, pattern
group and calibration -- this is an acknowledge, not a
repair. Consequence: bTaskFault is a PULSE, so the PLC
PLC tag -> logical task signal name.
Runtime output publishing also uses reverse lookup:
logical task signal name -> PLC tag.

Binary pattern images are not embedded directly in JSON.
ProjectRepository stores those cv::Mat images in project_images.
6 axes since Phase 5 (was 4: x, y, z, r).
The old 'r' and the new 'rz' are the SAME axis --
the rotation about Z -- so r was dropped and rz
carries it. rx / ry are genuinely new.
toString() emits six %08.2f fields per position, so
A robot program reading 4 fields per position does
not merely ignore the extras: it strides a flat field
list, so it MISALIGNS and reads wrong coordinates.
buildVisionOutputPositions() composes the world pose as
offset is applied in the TOOL frame.
x / y / z carry the composed translation.
rx / ry come straight from the pattern's rotation offset.
rz = worldYaw + offset.z -- the pick yaw and the pattern's
Z offset both act about Z, so they add into one axis.
At zero offset this reduces exactly to the pre-Phase-5
Rz translate, so existing patterns are unaffected: the
explicit owner, no QObject parent in runtime
